lesson_cards.summary: Learners should track confidence because confident wrong answers reveal hidden misconceptions.
lesson_cards.body: Teach each response as answer plus confidence: high, medium, or low. High-confidence wrong answers are reviewed first because the learner's internal rule is wrong. Low-confidence correct answers need reinforcement. High-confidence correct answers can move to spaced maintenance.
teaching_points: Correct with low confidence is still fragile.
Wrong with high confidence is the highest-priority review bucket.
Skipped items may be good pacing, not failure.
Confidence data helps Tutor choose the next lesson or drill.
quick_check_prompts: Which should be reviewed first: wrong with high confidence or wrong with low confidence?

lesson_cards.title: Entrance Exam error journal
lesson_cards.summary: An error journal turns wrong answers into specific future practice instead of vague discouragement.
lesson_cards.body: Teach a lightweight journal entry: section, item cue, selected method, error label, repair rule, and retest date. The journal should be short enough to use after every quick quiz. The goal is not paperwork; the goal is to make repeated patterns impossible to ignore.
teaching_points: Write the section first.
Name the item cue that should have triggered the method.
Name one repair rule.
Schedule one retest rather than rereading everything.
quick_check_prompts: What are the two most important fields in an Entrance Exam error journal?

lesson_cards.title: Elimination and educated guessing
lesson_cards.summary: When choices are present, elimination should be disciplined and tied to evidence or constraints.
lesson_cards.body: Teach educated guessing as a fallback after method work. Eliminate choices that violate units, passage evidence, direction tracing, or rough estimates. If two choices remain, choose the better-supported one, mark the uncertainty, and move on if pacing matters.
teaching_points: Eliminate impossible units or magnitudes first.
Reading choices must match passage evidence.
Visual choices must match the traced feature or direction.
A marked guess is better than losing time on several later easy items.
quick_check_prompts: Name one reason a choice can be eliminated before full calculation.

lesson_cards.title: Two-week entrance diagnostic map
lesson_cards.summary: A near-term learner needs a fast baseline, not a broad trade survey.
lesson_cards.body: Teach the learner to split preparation into five lanes: math setup, numerical pattern, reading evidence, mechanical trace, and spatial tracking. The first session should sample all five, then spend most daily time on the weakest two lanes while keeping a short mixed set every day.
teaching_points: Start with a timed mixed baseline before choosing drills.
Mark each miss with one primary tag: setup, arithmetic, misread, evidence, mechanical trace, spatial track, or pacing.
Do not postpone weak sections; rotate them daily in short blocks.
quick_check_prompts: For a test soon, what should the first study session produce: a weakness map, a contractor-law outline, a NEC article list, or a memorized answer sheet?

lesson_cards.title: No-calculator decimal arithmetic
lesson_cards.summary: Decimal placement and estimation protect many easy points.
lesson_cards.body: Teach decimal arithmetic with a three-step check: ignore decimals briefly, compute the whole-number shape, then place the decimal by magnitude. Before selecting an answer, estimate whether the result should be less than 1, between 1 and 10, or larger than 10.
teaching_points: Use estimation before exact arithmetic.
Align decimal places for addition and subtraction.
For multiplication, count decimal places after multiplying whole numbers.
quick_check_prompts: When multiplying 0.6 by 0.08, why should the answer be less than 0.1?

lesson_cards.title: Fractions, ratios, and proportions under time pressure
lesson_cards.summary: Most ratio errors come from comparing the wrong part to the wrong whole.
lesson_cards.body: Teach every ratio problem as parts first. Add the ratio parts to get the total parts, divide the real total by total parts, then multiply by the requested part. For percent problems, name the base before calculating.
teaching_points: In a ratio A:B, the whole is A+B parts unless the question says otherwise.
Percent change uses the original value as the base.
Cross-multiply only after writing matching units on both sides.
quick_check_prompts: In a 2:3 mix with 40 total items, why is one part worth 8?

lesson_cards.title: Algebra and function-table recognition
lesson_cards.summary: ETA-style samples make algebra/function practice a high-value preparation lane.
lesson_cards.body: Teach the learner to identify whether a question asks for substitution, solving for x, slope, pattern continuation, or function output. The safe routine is: copy the rule, substitute carefully, simplify one operation at a time, and check with estimation.
teaching_points: Function notation means input-output, not multiplication by a letter.
When solving equations, keep both sides balanced.
For tables, test differences, multiplication, and simple linear rules before guessing.
quick_check_prompts: If f(x)=3x+2, what does f(4) ask you to do?

lesson_cards.title: Gear and pulley direction tracing
lesson_cards.summary: Direction errors are preventable if the learner traces one contact at a time.
lesson_cards.body: Teach a one-connection rule: each pair of touching gears reverses direction; gears on the same shaft rotate together; crossed belts reverse direction while open belts usually keep direction. Draw arrows before thinking about speed.
teaching_points: Touching gears alternate direction.
Same-shaft parts share rotation direction.
Speed changes depend on relative size.
quick_check_prompts: If gear A touches gear B and B touches gear C, does C turn the same direction as A or opposite?

lesson_cards.title: Paper folding and hole-punch tracking
lesson_cards.summary: Spatial items reward slow, ordered unfolding.
lesson_cards.body: Teach the learner to reverse the folds one at a time. Each unfold mirrors the mark across the fold line. Do not rotate the mental picture unless the problem explicitly rotates the paper.
teaching_points: Reverse the last fold first.
Mirror across the fold line at each unfold.
Separate reflection from rotation.
quick_check_prompts: When unfolding a folded paper, should you reverse the first fold first or the last fold first?

lesson_cards.title: Personal Experience Form evidence stories
lesson_cards.summary: PEF preparation should collect honest evidence, not polished fiction.
lesson_cards.body: Teach the learner to organize experiences into situation, task, action, result, and evidence. Good entries show reliability, follow-through, math/technical exposure, teamwork, safety mindset, and learning attitude. The learner should not invent experience or copy generic wording.
teaching_points: Use real examples from work, school, volunteering, projects, or family responsibilities.
Attach evidence to claims: dates, role, supervisor, project, outcome.
Avoid exaggeration; consistency matters across application, PEF, and interview.
quick_check_prompts: What is stronger for PEF: a specific honest example or a vague claim that sounds impressive?

lesson_cards.title: Final 72-hour readiness routine
lesson_cards.summary: The final days should protect accuracy, sleep, documents, and confidence.
lesson_cards.body: Teach the learner to stop cramming broad new material. Use short mixed sets, review recurring error tags, prepare documents and route logistics, and sleep. The aim is stable performance, not exhausting practice volume.
teaching_points: Run short mixed practice, not marathon study.
Review the top three error tags and one fix for each.
Confirm ID, arrival time, address, parking, and permitted materials.
quick_check_prompts: In the final 72 hours, what matters more: stable accuracy and logistics, or learning every possible trade topic?

Keep the remediation task small enough to finish in one turn.

practice_blueprints.title: Worked-example ladder
practice_blueprints.summary: Generate a three-step worked example: model the first step, ask the learner for the next step, then ask a parallel multiple-choice item.
generation_rules: Use concrete numbers or facts only when they are original and source-safe.
Make the first example easier than the final quick check.
Explain why each distractor is attractive but wrong.
Use units and plain-language interpretation.

practice_blueprints.summary: Ask the learner to explain a concept in plain language, but allow a multiple-choice fallback when free response would slow momentum.
generation_rules: Use free response for concept consolidation, not as a mandatory gate after every mini-lesson.
Offer multiple-choice or true/false when the learner needs faster progress.
Require explain-back only for repeated misconceptions or readiness checkpoints.
Keep feedback direct and specific.

practice_blueprints.title: Mock debrief and next-plan generator
practice_blueprints.summary: After a sectional or mixed mock, generate a concise score review, top error tags, and the next three study actions.

Separate knowledge, calculation, reading, navigation, safety, and pacing errors.
Recommend the smallest useful next session.
Keep official exam logistics source-backed.

practice_blueprints.summary: Generate a short mixed review that includes one old mastered item, one recent lesson item, and one weak-tag remediation item.
generation_rules: Include at least one item from a previous module when possible.
Make review short enough to appear after a normal lesson.
Prefer multiple-choice or true/false for fast checks.
Use free response only when a concept needs explanation.

generation_rules: Use only original practice items, never recalled or copyrighted exam questions.
Start each drill with the method card for that section.
Require explanation only after repeated misses or at checkpoint moments.
Attach an error label to every wrong answer.

practice_blueprints.title: Entrance math without answer choices
practice_blueprints.summary: Generate numeric-fill arithmetic and algebra items so the learner cannot rely only on elimination.
generation_rules: Ask for the numeric answer first, then optionally show choices.
Keep arithmetic realistic for aptitude speed practice.

practice_blueprints.summary: Generate visual-thinking drills for levers, gears, pulleys, rotation, reflection, and paper folding.

Grade the reasoning step, not only the final letter.
Separate mechanical misses from spatial misses in the error log.

practice_blueprints.title: Entrance Exam section diagnostic matrix
practice_blueprints.summary: Generate a diagnostic that separately scores computation, math setup, numerical reasoning, reading evidence, mechanical tracing, spatial reasoning, pacing, and PEF/document readiness.
generation_rules: Use at least one non-multiple-choice item in math or spatial sections.
Do not collapse reading and numerical misses into a single score.
Recommend the next start point from the weakest repeated dimension.

practice_blueprints.title: Entrance Exam half mock
practice_blueprints.summary: Generate a medium-length mixed practice block for learners who are past basic method lessons but not ready for full mock pacing.

learning_activity_templates.title: Mini-lesson followed by one quick check
learning_activity_templates.summary: Default beginner flow for a new concept or procedure.
steps: State the practical job or exam situation in one paragraph.
Teach the smallest useful concept with one original example.
Register one four-option quick check with one best answer.
If correct, move to the next learning objective; if incorrect, explain the error pattern and ask one replacement check.
learner_action: Continue to the next objective after feedback.
feedback_rule: Do not ask the learner to choose the assessment format.
Do not chain multiple quizzes after a correct early answer.
Use free response only for review checkpoints, fragile understanding, or learner request.
exam_alignment: Matches multiple-choice exam rhythm while keeping Tutor teaching first.

learning_activity_templates.title: Worked example with hidden next step
learning_activity_templates.summary: Use for calculations, ratios, Ohm's Law, power, estimating, and blueprint arithmetic.
steps: Show the original scenario and identify known quantities.
Work the first step aloud.
Ask the learner to choose the next operation or expression.
Reveal the calculation and connect the result back to units and plausibility.
learner_action: Estimate whether the answer is reasonable.
feedback_rule: When the learner misses, identify whether the error was concept, setup, unit conversion, arithmetic, or answer-choice trap.
exam_alignment: Supports aptitude math, C-10 estimating math, and electrical calculation fluency.

learning_activity_templates.title: Open-book NEC navigation rehearsal
learning_activity_templates.summary: Use for GE objectives where the learner must look up code efficiently rather than rely only on memory.
steps: Present an original code-style scenario without copyrighted code text.
Ask the learner to classify the topic and predict the likely lookup area.
Ask what type of reference element matters: definition, article rule, table, note, or exception.
Close with a quick check about the navigation decision, not a copied code answer.
learner_action: Explain what evidence would confirm the answer.
feedback_rule: Track concept accuracy and lookup strategy separately.
Never reproduce NEC full text as course content.
exam_alignment: Matches GE open-book preparation where test materials are provided at the test site.

learning_activity_templates.title: Contractor scenario judgment
learning_activity_templates.summary: Use for C-10 trade judgment, Law & Business, safety, public works, contracts, liens, and employee topics.
steps: Present a realistic original contractor scenario.
Ask who has the obligation and what decision must be made.
Offer four answer choices with plausible distractors.
Explain why the best answer fits the role, timing, document, or safety obligation.
feedback_rule: Contrast the selected wrong answer with the best answer using one concrete distinction.
exam_alignment: Matches closed-book CSLB trade and Law & Business multiple-choice style without using leaked or recalled questions.

learning_activity_templates.title: Flashcard ladder for vocabulary and distinctions
learning_activity_templates.summary: Use when a learner needs fast recognition of terms before scenario practice.
steps: Show one term or pair of confusing terms.
Ask the learner to choose the best short meaning or distinction.
Promote correct cards into spaced review and keep missed cards in the current set.
After three correct cards, return to lesson or scenario practice.
feedback_rule: Keep flashcard sessions short; do not replace applied practice with memorization.
exam_alignment: Useful for vocabulary-heavy topics such as safety terms, plan symbols, business roles, and code navigation terms.

learning_activity_templates.title: Timed mixed set
learning_activity_templates.summary: Use after basic accuracy is stable, especially for aptitude, GE sectional practice, C-10, and Law & Business review.
steps: Select a small mixed set aligned to the current track.
Use a time budget that is short enough to reveal pacing habits.
Grade for accuracy and error type.
Send the learner back to the weakest lesson card or drill.
feedback_rule: Do timed sets only after the learner has seen the relevant mini-lessons.
Do not treat speed as mastery when conceptual accuracy is unstable.
exam_alignment: Supports timed aptitude preparation and later mock-exam readiness.

learning_activity_templates.title: Field visualization prompt
learning_activity_templates.summary: Use for circuits, raceways, boxes, panels, grounding, tools, jobsite safety, and troubleshooting.
steps: Describe a simple field situation with physical components.
Ask the learner to visualize current path, conductor route, equipment position, or hazard.
Change one condition and ask what changes.
Close with one safety or plausibility check.
learner_action: Predict the effect of changing one condition.
Connect the visual model to a rule or calculation.
feedback_rule: If the learner is confused, return to a simpler physical model before formulas.
exam_alignment: Supports mechanical reasoning, circuits, rough wiring, troubleshooting, and safety scenario questions.

learning_activity_templates.title: Document evidence coach
learning_activity_templates.summary: Use for PEF, GE experience, contractor qualifying experience, and learner readiness evidence.
steps: Ask the learner what claim they need to support.
List acceptable evidence categories at a high level without giving legal advice.
Separate documented, partially documented, and unsupported claims.
Create the next study or documentation task.
feedback_rule: Keep eligibility and documentation guidance separate from exam teaching.
Tell the learner to verify formal requirements with the official administering body.
exam_alignment: Supports application readiness for apprenticeship, GE, and contractor paths.

learning_activity_templates.title: Entrance Exam warmup ladder
learning_activity_templates.summary: A short daily warmup that moves from recall to calculation to one timed item before the main lesson.
steps: Ask one flashcard-style trigger question from the current section.
Ask one no-choice numeric or short-answer item.
Ask one timed multiple-choice item.
Tag the miss if any, then continue to the planned mini-lesson.
learner_action: Write the setup before arithmetic when math is involved.
Name the error pattern after feedback.
feedback_rule: Keep warmups under five minutes.
Do not block the lesson unless the same error repeats twice.
exam_alignment: Builds daily retrieval and pacing for aptitude-section readiness.

learning_activity_templates.title: Reading annotation drill
learning_activity_templates.summary: A passage-first drill where the learner marks controlling words before seeing or choosing the answer.
steps: Show a short original technical or admissions passage.
Ask the learner to identify the controlling phrase.
Ask a multiple-choice or short evidence question.
After grading, explain whether the miss was add, reverse, overstate, or ignore-condition.
learner_action: Underline mentally: only, except, before, after, must, may, not permitted.
Answer from the passage rather than outside knowledge.
feedback_rule: If the learner chooses an unsupported answer, require the controlling phrase on the replacement item.
exam_alignment: Supports reading-comprehension sections without using official passages.

learning_activity_templates.title: Mechanical visual trace board
learning_activity_templates.summary: A visual-thinking activity for levers, gears, pulleys, ramps, rotation, and paper folding.
steps: Name the system: lever, ramp, gear train, pulley, rotation, reflection, or fold.
Pick one feature, pivot, fold line, or gear contact to track.
Predict direction, force tradeoff, or final position before choices.
Grade the tracing step and the final answer separately.
learner_action: Move one connection or fold at a time.
Avoid jumping to the final image before tracing.
feedback_rule: If the final answer is right but tracing is wrong, mark as fragile and give one more visual trace.
exam_alignment: Supports mechanical comprehension and paper-folding/spatial readiness.

learning_activity_templates.title: Adaptive retest loop
learning_activity_templates.summary: A remediation loop that retests the exact skill behind a miss after one short repair explanation.
steps: Grade the learner's response as correct, incorrect, or fragile.
Assign one error label.
Teach a one-paragraph repair tied to that label.
Ask a new original item with the same underlying skill but different surface story.
learner_action: Apply the repair method on a new item.
Continue only after the repeated miss is resolved or scheduled for review.
feedback_rule: Never advance after a wrong answer without correction and a retest decision.
Avoid long free-response gates unless the learner repeatedly guesses.
exam_alignment: Turns quick quizzes into mastery evidence instead of simple exposure.

learning_activity_templates.title: Final-week mock block
learning_activity_templates.summary: A compressed mixed block for learners close to an Entrance Exam date, balancing speed, coverage, and document readiness.
steps: Run a short mixed set across math, numerical, reading, mechanical, and spatial items.
Have the learner mark confidence on each answer.
Grade by section and error label.
Close with one application or PEF/document readiness reminder.
learner_action: Do not spend too long on one visual item.
Review only the top two error types after the block.
feedback_rule: In final-week mode, prioritize repeated high-yield errors and test execution over broad new content.
exam_alignment: Builds near-term readiness for timed aptitude selection.

learning_activity_templates.title: Spaced error retest
learning_activity_templates.summary: Retest missed Entrance Exam skills after a delay and inside a mixed context.
steps: Select one recent repeated miss from the error journal.
Teach the repair rule in one paragraph.
Ask a new original item with the same underlying skill.
Schedule or run a mixed retest where the section is not announced.
learner_action: State the repair rule before answering.
Answer without relying on the previous surface story.
feedback_rule: Advance only when the learner succeeds on delayed or mixed retest, not just immediate retry.
exam_alignment: Supports durable readiness under mixed aptitude conditions.

learning_activity_templates.title: Confidence-marked quick quiz
learning_activity_templates.summary: A quick quiz where each answer includes confidence so Tutor can route review intelligently.
steps: Ask one to three original items.
Ask the learner to mark high, medium, or low confidence.
Grade correctness and confidence together.
Route to maintenance, reinforcement, misconception repair, or pacing practice.
learner_action: Accept a short review bucket label after grading.
feedback_rule: Review high-confidence wrong answers before low-confidence wrong answers.
exam_alignment: Improves mock review quality and reduces hidden misconceptions.

learning_activity_templates.title: Interleaved three-pack
learning_activity_templates.summary: Three short items from different Entrance Exam sections to train rapid method switching.
steps: Ask one math or numerical item.
Ask one reading evidence item.
Ask one mechanical or spatial item.
Compare the method cue for each item after grading.
learner_action: Use the matching method, not the method from the previous item.
feedback_rule: If the learner misclassifies two items, return to section triage before more mixed practice.
exam_alignment: Builds flexible performance across aptitude sections.

learning_activity_templates.title: Exam-day simulation
learning_activity_templates.summary: A rehearsal that includes pacing, instructions, uncertainty handling, and document readiness.
steps: Start with one instruction-reading check.
Run a timed mixed block.
Require skip/mark/return decisions when an item stalls.
Close with a short PEF or document readiness check.
learner_action: Protect easy points by moving on when stuck.
Record top errors and document gaps.
feedback_rule: Do not add new broad content during exam-day simulation; only repair repeated high-risk errors.
exam_alignment: Practices the behavior needed on selection day, not just isolated knowledge.

learning_activity_templates.title: Entrance daily rotation
learning_activity_templates.summary: A short daily block for learners with an exam soon.
steps: Run three easy arithmetic warmups.
Drill the weakest lane for 12-15 minutes.
Run a five-question mixed set.
Record one error tag and one fix.
learner_action: Review only missed or guessed items.
feedback_rule: Prefer immediate feedback.
Move on after one correct quick check unless confidence is low.
exam_alignment: Builds section switching and pacing for aptitude testing.

learning_activity_templates.title: Evidence-first reading drill
learning_activity_templates.summary: A technical reading routine that prevents unsupported-answer mistakes.
steps: Read the question before the passage.
Find the controlling sentence.
Predict the answer in plain language.
Select the matching option and cite the phrase.
learner_action: Provide an answer and the evidence phrase.
feedback_rule: Grade unsupported claims as reading-evidence errors even if they sound plausible.
exam_alignment: Matches reading-comprehension selection logic.

learning_activity_templates.title: Mechanical one-sketch trace
learning_activity_templates.summary: A visual trace routine for levers, gears, pulleys, and motion.
steps: Identify input, output, support, and contact points.
Draw one arrow at the input.
Propagate one connection at a time.
Answer only after the trace is complete.
learner_action: Explain the trace in one or two sentences.
feedback_rule: Correct direction errors by replaying the first wrong connection.
exam_alignment: Supports mechanical reasoning without requiring trade knowledge.

learning_activity_templates.title: Pacing and confidence lab
learning_activity_templates.summary: A timed block that trains skip, return, and confidence marking.
steps: Mark each answer as sure, maybe, or guessed.
Skip any item that exceeds the time budget.
Return after easier items are complete.
Review misses by accuracy and confidence.
feedback_rule: Prioritize high-confidence misses and slow correct answers in remediation.
exam_alignment: Builds reliable scoring behavior under time pressure.
